body:
On 2026-08-10 a sweep in the shared `repo/` checkout walked ~12 open PR branches in one
pattern -- checkout, merge main, commit, back to main, `pull --ff-only`, next -- and was
killed part-way through when the Mac rebooted at ~14:42Z.

**The deterministic floor does not do this.** `finish-armed-automerges.sh` refreshes a BEHIND
branch server-side via `gh api -X PUT repos/<repo>/pulls/<N>/update-branch`; it never checks
out a branch locally. No other script under `scripts/` performs a checkout+merge sweep over
open PRs (`draft-cherry-pick.sh` checks out, but only for a single upstream cherry-pick).
The commit messages are also hand-written prose -- e.g. `a83785086` "Merge main; collapse the
duplicate Fixed heading under [Unreleased]" -- where the floor writes templated ledger rows.
So the actor was phase-7 (`claude -p /CWNG-tick`), improvising branch maintenance, inside the
tick's 22-minute life before the reboot.

Two distinct harms, both observed:

1. **HEAD moves under concurrent sessions.** `repo/` is shared with interactive sessions.
   Two of them had HEAD change mid-command while reading or testing. The tick's own section 0
   exists to re-park a stray branch, which shows the design assumes `repo/` sits on the base --
   phase-7 checking out feature branches violates the invariant the floor then repairs.

2. **A half-applied sweep leaves branches carrying a stale resolution.** The sweep resolved the
   same CHANGELOG conflict on each branch it touched. It died mid-run, so some branches carry a
   resolution and some do not, and all of them predate the canonical fix that later landed
   (#1532). Merging any of them now silently re-creates the defect: `git merge-tree --write-tree`
   shows #1506, #1507 and #1515 all merging CLEAN with the entry duplicated, because two
   convergent edits produce no conflict. `test_no_section_repeats_a_kind_heading` does not catch
   it -- the headings are correct; the duplication is in the body.

Attribution caveat: every session authenticates as `new-usemame`, so neither git nor the API
can name the writer. "Not the deterministic floor" is proven from the code; "therefore phase-7"
rests on the timing window and the prose commit messages.

Suggested direction (not implemented): phase-7 should never check out a branch in `repo/`.
Give it a dedicated worktree, or push it toward the server-side `update-branch` the floor
already uses. A sweep that mutates N branches should also be resumable or transactional, so a
kill leaves none half-done rather than some.

Detection worth keeping regardless: before merging anything into a file two actors have
touched, simulate it --

    T=$(git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main origin/<branch> | head -1)
    git show "$T:CHANGELOG.md" | grep -c '<entry text>'   # expect 1

-- which inspects the merge result without performing it, and is the only instrument that sees
this class coming rather than afterwards.
title: Phase-7 mutates other sessions' branches in the shared repo/ checkout
